GENERALIZATION
A model generalizes when it performs well on new data it did not train on.

code.pseudocode:
Define the explicit rules a traditional program uses.
new_output <- apply_rules(input)

Collect examples that contain the useful input information.
examples <- collect_examples()

Use examples to learn a model instead of hard-coding every rule.
model <- learn(examples)
code.python:
examples = [(3, "small"), (14, "large"), (8, "small")]

# Learn a cut-off from the examples instead of hard-coding it
small = [x for x, label in examples if label == "small"]
large = [x for x, label in examples if label == "large"]
threshold = (max(small) + min(large)) / 2
print(threshold)  # 11.0

code.pseudocode:
Give the trained model a new example it has not seen.
new_example <- 12

Use the learned pattern to predict the new example.
prediction <- model.predict(new_example)
code.python:
threshold = 11.0  # learned from the examples in the previous step
new_example = 12
prediction = "large" if new_example > threshold else "small"
print(prediction)  # large
